title: Trapping Rain Water
cue: Water held above each bar: depends on the tallest bar on each side.
note: Water above i = min(max left, max right) − h[i]. Two pointers: move the side whose running max is smaller, because that side's water level is already fixed. #62 also moves the shorter side inward, but it maximises one container instead of summing water per column. #13's monotonic stack gives a layer-by-layer alternative.

title: Minimum Window Substring
cue: Shortest substring containing all required characters (with multiplicity).
note: **Near-duplicate of #268.** Need-counter plus a `formed` count: expand right until every requirement is met, then shrink left while it still holds, recording the best window.

title: Sliding Window Maximum
cue: Max of every window of size k, in O(n).
note: Fixed window like #26, but only the maximum is needed. Keep a deque of indices whose values are decreasing: pop smaller values from the back before pushing, and pop expired indices from the front. The front is the window max, in O(n) total instead of heaps.

title: Largest Rectangle in Histogram
cue: Largest rectangle under bars: each bar extends until a shorter bar on either side.
note: Uses #13's next-smaller machinery on **both** sides. Each bar's widest rectangle spans from its previous-smaller to its next-smaller index. An increasing stack finds both in one pass: popping a bar means its right boundary is found, and the new stack top is its left boundary.

title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
cue: Median of two sorted arrays in O(log(m+n)).
note: **Near-duplicate of #27.** Binary-search a cut in the shorter array so that both left parts together hold half the elements and max(left) ≤ min(right). Then the median comes from the four boundary values. O(log min(m, n)).

title: Merge K Sorted Lists
cue: Merge k sorted sequences into one.
note: k-way merge, a sibling of #5's order statistics across sorted inputs. Keep a min-heap of (value, list index, node) holding each list's current head; pop the smallest and push its successor, O(N log k). Pairwise divide-and-conquer merging is the alternative without a heap. Add the list index as a tie-breaker, because nodes can't be compared.

title: Reverse Nodes in k-Group
cue: Reverse every full block of k nodes, and leave the short tail as it is.
note: **Near-duplicate of #251.** Run #506's pointer-reversal loop on each full block of k nodes, reconnecting each block through a dummy head and the previous block's tail. Check that k nodes remain before reversing.

title: Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum
cue: Best path between any two nodes, where values can be negative.
note: A post-order "return a summary" problem, like #372 and the #354 diameter template. Each node returns its best downward chain, clamped at 0 so negative branches are dropped. The answer is updated at every node with left + node + right.

title: Serialize and Deserialize Binary Tree
cue: Convert a tree to a string and back.
note: #305 rebuilds from two traversals and needs distinct values. Here a **single** preorder with null markers is enough, because the markers fix the shape. Deserialize recursively from an iterator. Level-order with nulls also works.

title: Word Search II
cue: Find all dictionary words on a letter grid.
note: #91 walks a trie along 1-D text. Here you DFS the grid **while** walking the trie: stop when no child matches, mark found words and delete exhausted branches so they aren't reported twice, and restore visited cells on backtrack.

title: Find Median from Data Stream
cue: Insert numbers and query the median at any time.
note: **Near-duplicate of #216.** Use a max-heap for the lower half and a min-heap for the upper half. After each insert, rebalance so the sizes differ by at most 1.

title: N-Queens
cue: Place n queens so none attack each other, and list every board.
note: **Near-duplicate of #296.** Place one queen per row, with O(1) conflict checks using sets for columns, diagonals (r − c) and anti-diagonals (r + c).

title: Word Ladder
cue: Fewest one-letter changes from start word to end word.
note: The count-only version of #388. BFS by layers from the start word, using wildcard buckets (`h*t`) to find neighbours in O(L) lookups, and return the layer number when the end word is reached. No path reconstruction is needed.

title: Reconstruct Itinerary
cue: Use every ticket exactly once, and pick the smallest lexical order.
note: **A new concept not in the PracHub set: Eulerian path** (use every edge once). Hierholzer's algorithm: DFS that always takes the smallest remaining outgoing ticket (a sorted list or heap per airport). Append the airport only once its edges are used up, then reverse the result.

title: Swim in Rising Water
cue: Minimise the highest cell on a path from corner to corner.
note: **Same minimax path as #200**: a path's cost is its highest cell. Three ways to solve it: Dijkstra with `max` instead of `+`, binary search on the time plus a BFS reachability check, or Union-Find adding cells in increasing height until the corners connect.

title: Alien Dictionary
cue: Recover the letter order from a sorted list of words.
note: The new part is building the graph. Compare each adjacent pair of words: the first differing letters give one edge. If a longer word comes before its own prefix, the input is invalid. Then run Kahn's algorithm as in #6; a cycle means no valid order. Use a heap, as in #67, if the order must be deterministic.

title: Longest Increasing Path in a Matrix
cue: Longest strictly increasing path moving in 4 directions on a grid.
note: **Near-duplicate of #430.** Memoised DFS: the strictly increasing rule makes the grid a DAG, so no visited set is needed. Each cell's answer is 1 plus the best answer among its larger neighbours.

title: Distinct Subsequences
cue: Count the ways t appears as a subsequence of s.
note: Two-sequence DP like #416, but **counting** instead of optimising. dp[i][j] is the number of ways to form t[:j] from s[:i]. It always includes dp[i−1][j] (skip s[i−1]), plus dp[i−1][j−1] when the characters match (use it). Base case: dp[i][0] = 1.

title: Burst Balloons
cue: Maximise coins from bursting balloons; each burst depends on its current neighbours.
note: **Near-duplicate of #508.** Interval DP: pick which balloon in (l, r) is burst **last**. Its neighbours are then l and r, which splits the range into two independent subproblems. Pad the array with 1s at both ends.

title: Regular Expression Matching
cue: Full match with `.` and `*`.
note: **Near-duplicate of #60.** Two-string DP. When p[j] is followed by `*`, either skip the pair (zero copies) or consume one matching character of s and stay on the same pattern position. The base row handles patterns like `a*b*` matching an empty string.

title: Minimum Interval to Include Each Query
cue: For each query point, the size of the smallest interval containing it.
note: Offline sweep: sort intervals by start and queries by value. For each query, push every interval with start ≤ q into a min-heap keyed by size, and pop those with end < q; the heap top is the answer. Related to #260's containing-range lookup, but this wants the *smallest* containing interval for many queries. Answer the queries in their original order.
